parts.title: Glutes
parts.description: The glutes are a muscle group consisting of three muscles, the well known gluteus maximus, which is the largest and strongest muscle in the human body, gluteus medius, and gluteus minimus. The muscles extend and abduct the legs, as well as making external rotation of the hip possible and providing support for the extended knee.

parts.title: Quads
parts.description: The quads are the legs' version of the tricep. A very strong muscle group working to extend the knee, just like the tricep extends the arm, along with it's another task, which is to flex the hip up towards the body. The quads are located on the front of the thigh and consists of four muscles, hence the name quads: rectus femoris, vastus medialis, vastus lateralis, and vastus intermedius.

parts.title: Lower leg muscles
parts.description: The lower leg muscles work in practically the same way as the forearm muscles — they are responsible for all foot movement like bringing the foot downwards towards the floor, rotating the foot, arching and inarching the foot and also bringing the foot upwards towards the ceiling. The calfs are the largest lower leg muscles and consists of the three muscles Gastrocnemius, Soleus and Plantaris. On the front of the lower legs we find the shins, where the tibialis sits along with a whole complex of muscles.

parts.title: Chest
parts.description: The chest's task is to push the arms forward and away from the body. The chest is a very large and powerful muscle group consisting of three parts: the upper, the middle and the lower head.

parts.title: Abs
parts.description: The abs are part of the core muscle group, and are a chain of muscles responsible for pulling the upper body towards the legs and vice versa. This plays a big part in stabilising the upper body and strengthening the core. The abs consists of the rectus abdominis which are the infamous six pack.

parts.title: External Obliques
parts.description: The oblique muscles are also part of the core, and their main function is to pull the upper body sidewards towards the legs and vice versa. The obliques do a large part in stabilising the core as they are located on the sides preventing the upper body from swaying from side to side — imagine them as the wires on a radio tower, dragging on each side to hold the body upright.

parts.title: Shoulder Deltoids
parts.description: The shoulder is the second largest arm muscle and is responsible for moving the shoulder joint, doing both push and pulling. The shoulder muscles are naturally located on the shoulders and consists of three parts: the anterior head on the front side, the lateral head in the middle, and the posterior head on the back side.

parts.title: Biceps Brachii
parts.description: The biceps is the third largest arm muscle. Its main task is to retract the arm, pulling the hand towards the shoulders. The bicep is, as its name states, built up of two parts: the long head located furthest out from the chest, and the short head located on the inside of the arm closest to the chest.

parts.title: Triceps Brachii
parts.description: The tricep is the largest arm muscle and is responsible for straightening out the elbow making the arm as long as possible. The tricep consists of three parts: the long head located under the arm, the lateral head on the side of the arm, and the medial head closest to the elbow.

parts.title: Forearms
parts.description: The forearms are a complex muscle group consisting of a whole list of heads. They allow for movement of the hands as well as the elbows, wrists and fingers. The forearm muscles are located between the elbow and the wrist.

parts.title: Traps
parts.description: The trap is a star-shaped muscle that stretches from the lats and all the way up to the neck, as well as out to each shoulder. The trap muscle has a lot of responsibility: it tilts the head up and down, turns it from side to side, maintains your posture, moves the shoulders both backwards and upwards and twists the torso.

parts.title: Middle back
parts.description: The middle back is a muscle group consisting of three different muscles. The muscle group supports posture, stabilizes the spine and enables shoulder blade movement.

parts.title: Lats
parts.description: The lats are the largest back muscles and are responsible for arm movement like pulling the arms down towards the sides of body, pulling them backwards, as well as rotating the arms inwards towards each other.
